summary: Warm-cache initialization line on finalized invoice after KMS key rotation on private VPC
description: Issue summary: Customer saw a $1,250 'warm-cache initialization' invoice line on their finalized monthly invoice for their private VPC deployment after a scheduled KMS key rotation. They expected reserved-hours credits to offset warmup charges for private deployments. Impact: unexpected invoice charge, finance team escalation, autopay blocked pending dispute. Environment: private deployment (VPC-connected control plane), prod region us-east-1, KMS rotation performed 2026-02-27 03:15 UTC. Customer provided invoice PDF and a snippet of their deployment logs that show a brief VPN reconnection and a set of postbacks with tag 'warmup' within the KMS rotation window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer rotated KMS key for private control plane on 2026-02-27 03:15 UTC. 2) Private connector experienced a VPN rekey and transient TLS reconnect for ~90s. 3) Serving instances restarted and triggered KV cache warmup; postbacks emitted to billing ingester with tag 'warmup-init'. 4) Billing system later finalized invoice and did not apply reserved-hour buffer credits for the warmup line. Note: customer says reserved-hours are active and applied correctly elsewhere on invoice.
logs_and_links: Customer provided: invoice PDF (INV-NTW-2026-02.pdf). Deployment logs excerpt: s3://nextwave-prod/logs/kms_rotation_2026-02-27.txt. Billing ingestion trace: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/ingest-traces/trace-9a8b7c. Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123SUPPORT/p1677490000000. Console screenshot: https://console.redwood.company/screenshots/nextwave/invoice-warmup-0226.png
comments: 2026-03-01 09:12 - Sofia Martinez (Support): Customer reports warmup init charge $1,250 appears on finalized invoice INV-NTW-2026-02. Says reserved-hours on private deployment should cover warm-cache. Customer requests immediate provisional credit while we investigate.
2026-03-01 09:35 - Jordan Lee (Billing ENG): Acknowledged ticket. I'm pulling ingestion traces and will correlate postback tags to reserved-hour matching logic. Assigned to me for triage.

2026-03-01 11:02 - Priya Shah (SRE - Private Deploy): SRE note: there was a KMS rotation on 2026-02-27 03:15 UTC for NextWave's private control plane. Private connector did a rekey and re-established tunnels. I see restart events on 3 serving nodes between 03:16:02 and 03:17:45. Possible duplicate warmup postbacks emitted.

2026-03-01 14:20 - Jordan Lee (Billing ENG): Investigation: Ingestion trace shows three postbacks with tag 'warmup-init' from private connector during the reconnection window. Postbacks omitted the reserved-hours tag due to transient metadata fetch failure (500 from control-plane metadata API) at 03:16:06-03:16:12. Billing matching logic only applies reserved-hours when postback contains 'reserved_hours=true' attribute. Missing attribute explains why warmup line was billed.

2026-03-02 08:45 - Jordan Lee (Billing ENG): Applied provisional credit $1,250 to customer account as a temporary fix and added invoice memo. Customer notified via email. Creating follow-up internal bug for metadata fetch resiliency.

2026-03-02 10:12 - Lauren Park (Customer - NextWave): Thanks — we received the provisional credit and will confirm with finance. Please advise on permanent fix and whether this will recur on future rotations.

2026-03-03 16:40 - Priya Shah (SRE): Root cause hypothesis: during KMS rekey the control plane briefly rejected metadata requests for private connectors (error rate spike). Private connector retried and sent warmup postbacks but without reserved-hours metadata. Added link to trace and sample postback payload: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/ingest-traces/sample-payload-9a8b7c

2026-03-03 16:55 - Jordan Lee (Billing ENG): Mitigation plan: (1) Backfill: create a reconciler job to consume postback raw payloads for the 5-minute window around KMS rotations and reapply reserved tag where applicable; (2) Fix: change billing ingester to fallback to account-level reserved-hours lookup if postback metadata is missing; (3) Add alert on metadata API 5xx spikes. Created internal support task INT-207101 for the ingester fallback work.

2026-03-03 17:05 - Lauren Park (Customer): Confirmed finance sees provisional credit on their account; requests timeline for permanent fix and whether similar credits will be needed for previous rotations this quarter.

2026-03-03 17:20 - Jordan Lee (Billing ENG): We will run a backfill for previous KMS rotation windows this week and follow up with a CSV of any additional credits applied. ETA for ingester fallback patch: 2 sprints (target 2026-03-25).
investigation_notes: Initial correlation shows metadata API 500 errors coincident with KMS rotation led to missing 'reserved_hours' attribute on billing postbacks. Billing matching service requires attribute for automatic credit application. Evidence: ingestion trace IDs 9a8b7c, 9a8b7d; sample payloads show 'warmup-init' + no reserved_hours key. SRE confirmed three restarts and a 90s transient tunnel rekey. Reproducer: simulate metadata API 500 and confirm warmup postback lacks reserved flag and gets billed. Potential edgecases: private control plane rotation path has short-lived auth token renewal that can return 503, causing metadata fetch to fail in the connector's warmup path.
resolution: Temporary resolution: provisional credit of $1,250 applied on 2026-03-02 and invoice memo added. Backfill scheduled to scan 7 days of postbacks around 2026-02-27 to find similar missed reserved-hours tagging and apply credits if found. Permanent fix: billing ingester to fallback to account-level reserved-hours lookup when postback metadata missing (INT-207101). Added metadata API 5xx alert and runbook to avoid missing tags during planned KMS work. Customer notified of plan and ETA. Follow-up: runbook update for Private KMS rotation to sequence metadata refresh before connector warmup triggers.
